classification.difficultyReason: Compare the structural restrictions of two procedures for generating Pythagorean triples.

inlines.text: Pythagoras’ method starts with an odd side length, squares it and subtracts 1, then halves the result to obtain the second side. Adding 1 to the second side gives the hypotenuse. Plato’s method starts with a side length divisible by 4; squaring it, dividing by 4 and subtracting 1 gives the second side, while squaring it, dividing by 4 and adding 1 gives the hypotenuse.
Again, not all Pythagorean triples can be produced in this way. For example, 77, 36, 85 is a Pythagorean triple. Can you see why it does not fit Plato’s method or Pythagoras’ method?

answer.short: Neither method produces this triple. Pythagoras’ method requires the hypotenuse and one other side to differ by 1; Plato’s method requires them to differ by 2. Here the differences are $85-77=8$ and $85-36=49$.
answer.worked:
Pythagoras’ method makes the hypotenuse 1 greater than the second side. Plato’s method makes the hypotenuse 2 greater than the second side.

The hypotenuse of the given triple is 85. Comparing it with both other sides:
$$\begin{align*}85-77&=8\\85-36&=49\end{align*}$$
Neither difference is 1 or 2, so the triple cannot be produced by either method.
